monotonicity_verdict.question: Does C.InextensibleNestedOn C' W with V ≤ W give C.InextensibleNestedOn C' V? (the ladder's `what`, programme/ladder.toml:854: 'not known to pass to a smaller open')
monotonicity_verdict.verdict: False in general. Refuted in Lean on a space that is not T1. On a Hausdorff, second countable space it is false by an argued example that is not in Lean. With both causalities causal it is open.

lean_refutation.witness: Causal.CoarsePoint.separates_inextensibleNestedOn_mono (scaffold/CausalScaffold/InextensibleNestedBasics.lean:507): CoarsePoint.nearOpens ≤ ⊤ ∧ (LineDevelopment.allRelated CoarsePoint).InextensibleNestedOn CoarsePoint.diag ⊤ ∧ ¬ (LineDevelopment.allRelated CoarsePoint).InextensibleNestedOn CoarsePoint.diag CoarsePoint.nearOpens ∧ (∀ W, (allRelated CoarsePoint).AbsolutelyMinimalOn W) ∧ (∀ W, diag.AbsolutelyMinimalOn W) ∧ diag.IsCausal
lean_refutation.space: Causal.CoarsePoint has two near points (near false, near true) and a far point far S for each S : Set ℝ. Its open sets are ∅, the two near points (nearOpens) and everything. The space is not T1 (not even T0). It is second countable, with three open sets, but this is not proved in Lean. Every precausality on it is absolutely minimal on every open set (CoarsePoint.absolutelyMinimalOn), so the witness stands in either form of DEC-167's gluing. allRelated is not causal; diag (each point related only to itself) is causal.
lean_refutation.how: At M the nesting is vacuous: no causal curve of allRelated is inextensible (CoarsePoint.allRelated_extensible, scaffold/CausalScaffold/InextensibleNestedBasics.lean:438). By Cantor, the image of a curve misses some far point. Squeezing the parameters below π/2 by arctan (Extensible.of_comp) and appending that far point at parameter 2 gives an extension, with a pause at the last point when there is one, because the near points form an open set. On nearOpens, the step (near false up to time 0, near true after) is inextensible for allRelated, because its image is all of nearOpens. It is not a causal curve of diag, because it jumps at 0.

monotonicity_verdict.argued_T2_counterexample_not_in_Lean: Take the circle ℝ/3ℤ. Let C' be clockwise motion (not causal). Let C be clockwise motion that never passes a point p: x ≤ y iff the clockwise arc (x, y] misses p, and x ≪ y asks moreover x ≠ p, so that I⁻ stays open (not cutLine's convention carried to the circle, under which C is not causal). C is causal; the relations are not in Lean. Let V be the circle minus a point q ≠ p. A C-curve never passes p, so its lift moves by less than a turn and has a limit at both ends. Such a curve extends at an end unless that end is its start at p or its approach to p. So every C-inextensible curve of the circle starts at p and comes back to it. Its image is the whole circle, so it is C'-inextensible. In V, the arc from p clockwise to q is C-inextensible, and C' extends it at p from the other side.
monotonicity_verdict.why: An inextensible curve of V need not be one of W, since it may extend out of V, and nothing ties the C'-extensions inside V to the C-inextensible curves of W. In the Lean example the nesting at M is vacuous (no inextensible curve of allRelated exists there); in the circle example the C-inextensible curves of W cover p, through which C' extends the V-curve. Whether the route closes when C and C' are both causal on a T2, second countable space is open (a heuristic, not proved).
